question.text:
You are analyzing two real estate investment trusts (REITs) over the last year: REIT X: Total Return = 12%, Dividend Yield = 4% REIT Y: Total Return = 15%, Dividend Yield = 3.5%
Which REIT has the higher share of total return coming from dividend yield (i.e., income as a proportion of total return)?

answer.text: Both REITs have the same share
Cannot determine from the given data

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, REITs distribute earnings as dividends, and total return is defined as income plus change in value. Computing the share of total return delivered as income: REIT X = 4% / 12% = 33.3%, and REIT Y = 3.5% / 15% = 23.3%. REIT X has the higher income share of total return. The Trap: Candidates who anchor on REIT Y's higher absolute 15% total return assume a bigger pie means a bigger income share. "Same" and "cannot determine" tempt those who skip the proportion step. Note: Dividend yield ÷ total return is a share, not the accounting "dividend payout ratio" (which would be dividend ÷ earnings). The question is framed as the proportion of total return that is income.
